meta.question: Does Sint Maarten still have damage?

question: Does Sint Maarten still have damage?

answers: Yes, Sint Maarten was significantly impacted by Hurricane Irma, with about 70% of its houses destroyed or severely damaged. The extent of the damage has led to thousands of residents seeking shelter, and it is expected that at least € 1 billion ( $1.2 billion ) will be required for restoration efforts. The airport and harbor suffered damage as well, leaving the Dutch part of Saint Martin unreachable, though the smaller Grand Case - Espérance Airport on the French side was reopened for supply aid. The Dutch military assisted in evacuating people and providing warnings for Hurricane Jose.

When was the Netherlands Golden Age?

The Netherlands experienced a Golden Age c. 1590s -- 1720s. A technological revolution in shipbuilding led to a competitive advantage in shipping that helped the young Republic become the dominant trade power by the mid-17th century. From about 1600 to 1720, the Dutch had the highest per capita income in the world, at least double that of neighbouring countries at the time.
How important was shipping for the economy?

Shipping played a significant role in the Dutch economy during their Golden Age. A technological revolution in shipbuilding gave the Dutch a competitive advantage in shipping, which helped them become the dominant trade power by the mid-17th century. By 1670, the Dutch merchant marine totaled 568,000 tons of shipping, which was about half the European total. The VOC 's shipyards also contributed greatly to the Dutch domination of global shipbuilding and shipping industries during the 1600s.
Which products did the Dutch East India Company ( VOC ) bring back?

Ships arriving in Batavia from the Netherlands brought supplies for the VOC (Dutch East India Company) settlements in Asia. Silver and copper from Japan were used to trade with India and China for silk, cotton, porcelain, and textiles. These products were then either traded within Asia for valuable spices or brought back to Europe. Starting in 1609, the VOC established a trading post in Japan, located in Hirado and Nagasaki, where local paper was used for administrative purposes. This paper was also traded with the VOC's other trading posts and even sent to the Dutch Republic. Many of the prints created by the Dutch Golden Age artist Rembrandt were made on Japanese paper.

The Dutch colonization of the Americas began with trading posts and plantations, predating their more famous activities in Asia. The first Dutch fort in Asia was established in 1600 in present-day Indonesia, but the earliest forts and settlements along the Essequibo River in Guyana date back to the 1590s. Dutch colonization was not as extensive as that of other European nations, and many settlements were lost or abandoned by the end of the 17th century. Nonetheless, the Netherlands retained Suriname until its independence in 1975 and still holds the Netherlands Antilles.
The loss of New Netherland contributed to the Second Anglo-Dutch War (1665-1667), ending with the Treaty of Breda, which required the Dutch to give up New Netherland in exchange for Suriname.
In South Africa, the Dutch established a significant presence, with Jan van Riebeeck founding Cape Town in 1652. 
A second wave of Dutch emigration to Chile occurred in 1895, when several families settled in Chiloé. Among them was Hageman Egbert, who arrived with his family in 1896, as well as the Wennekool family, who began the Dutch colonization of Villarrica.

Many former Dutch colonies have gained their independence and are now sovereign nations. However,  the Netherlands Antilles still retain ties to the Kingdom of the Netherlands. These include Aruba, Curaçao, and Sint Maarten in the Caribbean, which are constituent countries within the kingdom. Additionally, the Caribbean islands of Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, and Saba are special municipalities of the Netherlands.
Was Sint Maarten hit by a hurricane?

Hurricane Irma's intense winds ripped through buildings and lifted vehicles aloft as if they were matches. The hurricane wreaked havoc on Princess Juliana International Airport, with huge chunks of the building ( strewn ) across the runway and a jet bridge snapped in half. It demolished or severely damaged about 70 % of Sint Maarten 's houses, forcing thousands of residents into public shelters. The following day, Dutch military was able to airlift dialysis patients off the island while also dropping leaflets to warn islanders about the rapidly approaching Hurricane Jose. In addition to the airport, St. Maarten's harbor was damaged, making part of the island unreachable.
